recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is; the current build source already satisfies FHIR-16906, and further wording changes would be redundant rather than corrective.
issue_request: FHIR-16906 asked to rename or redefine Bundle.timestamp because its meaning was unclear and to clarify whether paged searchset Bundles must have different timestamps; the Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution clarified that different pages MAY have different timestamps but need not and that timestamp is the time the Bundle was assembled.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 14360, represented in git by 722bf2f4e92f86bb0907717922669ee10fb36d9c, which changed the Bundle.timestamp searchset usage note from 'different pages will have different timestamps' to 'different pages MAY have different timestamps but need not' in source/bundle/bundle-spreadsheet.xml. The assembled-time short/definition was already in the Bundle source lineage and was carried forward.
additional_context: The current source has since moved from spreadsheet-derived input into source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml, and source/fhir.ini lists Bundle as an active resource. FHIR-17055 is a same-family follow-up that added the no-implication sentence for different searchset page timestamps and is already represented on the combined branch. No relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. source/bundle/structuredefinition-Bundle.xml already says Bundle.timestamp is when the bundle was assembled, defines it as the date/time the bundle was assembled, and states that searchset pages MAY have different timestamps but need not.

related_jiras.note: Later Bundle.timestamp searchset tracker added that different page timestamps do not imply subsequent pages include changes made since the initial query; it is already audited on the combined branch.
